_stagger_comment: G0b (owner, 2026-09-17): how long a company takes to materialise, in seconds. Everything that decides the company -- its point, its packed spots, the cap it pays -- happens when it is seated; this spreads only *when* each body appears, oldest first, with the last landing as the window closes. 0 is a supported value and means the whole company on one frame. The point is that forty bodies appearing on a single frame is a pop however well spaced they are; 0.35 s is short enough to read as an arrival rather than a trickle. A number to revisit in the balance pass now that companies are the unit.
_unused_comment: Enemies benched from the run (owner, 2026-09-17). An id listed here keeps its block in `enemies.json`, its art, its rig, its weights in the bands below and every reference the code and the tests make to it -- it is *disabled*, not deleted. `SpawnTables` drops it from the phase types and the group followers when it reads them, so the director can never roll it; `spawn_at`, `spawn_group` and the dev menu can still seat one deliberately. Re-enabling is deleting a string from this list. Being absent from every band is NOT the same thing: Bonepicker, Gaffjaw and the Hammer Gnome are built and waiting for a band weight, which is pending work rather than a decision to bench them. The list is EMPTY as of G1 (owner, 2026-09-17): Stoutpaw was unbenched to join the Wild beasts group, and nothing is benched today. The mechanism stays -- it is one string away from being needed again -- and `tests/spawn/test_unused_category.py` exercises it against a synthetic table so it keeps working while the shipped list is empty.
_groups_comment: The six social groups a company is drawn from (G2, owner 2026-09-17). A company is ONE group: a count rolled in `common_range`, each body drawn by `commons` weight, plus -- on the two groups that have them -- elites drawn by `elites` weight. `elite_range` is [base minimum, ceiling] and `elite_step` is how much the minimum climbs every `cooldowns.step_seconds`, so an elite group's count is deterministic and growing while WHICH elites appear stays random. Weights are relative within their own half of a group and need not sum to anything. This replaced the old leader+followers templates outright, which is why the key is reused rather than renamed: a company has no leader, only a body that happens to be seated first. Clearance is no longer declared per group -- placement derives it from the largest body in the company, which is what the old `clearance` knob was approximating.
_common_cap_comment: G8 (owner, 2026-09-20): the most commons a company may carry, climbing through the run the way the elite ladder does. The cap is `start` + `step` per director step (`cooldowns.step_seconds`, compressed by the difficulty's timeline pace like everything else), never above `ceiling`; at composition a group's `common_range` is clipped to it at both ends, so early companies are small whatever the group declares and the declared range is reached once the cap passes it. Elite counts are not touched by this. A missing or malformed block means no cap, logged, never a refusal to load.
_cooldowns_comment: The two ladders (G2, owner 2026-09-17). `common` is how long before the next company of any kind; `elite` is a gate on ELIGIBILITY -- an elite-bearing group can only be picked when it is ready, and picking one resets both timers, so an elite and a common company never land back to back. Every `step_seconds` the common cadence drops by `common_decay` and the elite gate by `elite_decay`, flooring at `common_floor` / `elite_floor`; the gate falls three times as fast and floors three times higher, so elite companies go from about one in three to roughly one in one-and-a-bit by minute eight. `elite_unlock` is a hard gate: no elite group at all before then, whatever the ladder says. `cap_retry` is how long the master waits before re-counting when a prepared company does not fit under the live cap. Everything here is in Normal seconds and is divided by `timeline_pace` -- the STEP as well as the values, so the whole ladder compresses together rather than just its numbers. Because the step and the boss time scale by the same factor, every difficulty reaches the same elite count at its boss: harder means the same elites sooner, not more of them.
_population_comment: The ring (owner, 2026-09-18/19). A live body further than `despawn_radius` from the hero is hibernated whatever island it stands on and whether or not it is chasing -- distance wins, which is what stops a tail of abandoned bodies holding live-cap slots the player will never meet. A record is woken again when the hero comes within `wake_radius`. The gap between the two is hysteresis: without it a body pacing the boundary would sleep and wake on alternate ticks. 1400 clears every floor it has to -- placement seats a company at most 1100 px out, the 16:9 camera half-diagonal is 612, and the widest `aggro_range` in the roster is 640 -- so nothing is ever released inside the view or while it could still see the hero. 1100 is `far_max_distance` itself, so a record wakes exactly when it re-enters the band a company would be seated into. `dormant_cap` is a safety rail rather than a tuning number: records are bounded in practice by what the player has generated and walked away from, and the measured peak is 20 for a hero who stands still, 22 for one who patrols and 1304 for one teleporting between every island for five minutes -- the pessimistic case, and still a quarter of the cap. Past it the oldest-slept record is dropped, so an island abandoned longest ago is the one that forgets its population. At ~515 bytes a record the cap is about 2 MB.

placement._band_comment: Placement is a distance band around the hero, regardless of the camera (owner, 2026-09-15): the same request lands the same way at 16:9, 21:9, or with the view anywhere. The strict rung (FAR) takes a point between `far_min_distance` and `far_max_distance` from the hero -- 700 sits just past the 16:9 half-diagonal of 612 world px plus the old 96 px pad, so a 16:9 player still sees nothing appear, while a wider view may see an arrival at its edge; 1100 keeps the walk short. The middle rung (NEAR: a pack whose debt has aged past `relax_after`, or the strict rung empty) drops the ceiling and keeps `near_min_distance` as the keep-away.
placement._starved_comment: The last rung of the relaxation ladder, used only when no point passes the stricter rules -- which is what a player who camps on one island produces: its handful of points are all either on cooldown or inside the keep-away, and every pack becomes debt. At this rung the point cooldown shortens, so the same few points can be reused, and `starved_min_distance` is the only keep-away, so an enemy arrives at the edge of the screen rather than in the hero's lap; candidates here are also weighted by distance, which biases the draw outward.
placement._pack_comment: How a company is seated around its leader (G0a, 2026-09-17). Concentric rings spaced by a body diameter plus `pack_gap`; each body is then nudged up to `pack_jitter` of a cell in a random direction, retried `pack_tries` times before the exact slot is used, so the group reads as a crowd rather than as circles. `pack_spread` sizes the disc for the company -- start + step * spread * sqrt(n), a ceiling of about 275 px for forty small bodies (they in fact seat inside 174) and the `pack_max_radius` cap for thirty-odd large ones. Measured on a booted run: jitter at 0.35 costs nothing in fill and gains a little on large bodies, because a nudged candidate finds ground the exact slot missed; past 0.35 the fill starts to slip.
